content: Co-trimoxazole is a medication that combines two active ingredients, trimethoprim and sulfamethoxazole, which belong to the sulfa drug class. It works by eliminating bacteria responsible for various infections, such as urinary tract infections, pneumonia (lung infections), ear infections, and intestinal infections. It is also used to treat travelers' diarrhea. However, it is important to note that antibiotics like co-trimoxazole are ineffective against viral infections, such as colds or the flu. If you have questions about other potential uses of this medication, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Co-trimoxazole is available in tablet form and as a liquid for oral use. It is typically taken twice daily, but in cases of severe lung infections, it may be prescribed up to four times a day. Each dose should be taken with a full glass of water. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. It is crucial to take co-trimoxazole exactly as prescribed. Do not take more or less of the medication or use it more frequently than directed by your doctor. Before starting co-trimoxazole, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to this medication, any sulfa drugs, diuretics (commonly referred to as water pills), oral diabetes medications, or any other drugs. Additionally, provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are currently taking, especially methotrexate, phenytoin (Dilantin), warfarin (Coumadin), and any vitamins. Let your doctor know if you have a history of liver or kidney disease, asthma, severe allergies, or glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G-6-PD) deficiency, which is an inherited blood disorder. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. Should you become pregnant while taking co-trimoxazole, contact your doctor immediately. Wear protective clothing, sunglasses, and sunscreen when outdoors. Co-trimoxazole may cause stomach upset. To minimize this, take the medication with food. If you forget to take a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Co-trimoxazole may cause side effects. Minor side effects include upset stomach, vomiting, and loss of appetite. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects require immediate medical attention and include skin rash, itching, sore throat, fever or chills, mouth sores, unusual bruising or bleeding, yellowing of the skin or eyes, paleness, and joint pain. If you experience a severe side effect, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store co-trimoxazole in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all scheduled appointments with your doctor and laboratory, as your doctor may order tests to monitor your response to co-trimoxazole. Do not share this medication with others, and note that your prescription is likely not refillable. If your symptoms persist after completing the prescribed course, contact your doctor. Co-trimoxazole is sold under several brand names, including Bactrim®, Bactrim® DS, Septra®, Septra® DS, Septra® Grape Suspension, Septra® Suspension, Sulfatrim® Pediatric Suspension, and Sulfatrim® Suspension.
